title: The variable that is not the variable you meant

prereqs.why: The bug is a shadowed name, which only makes sense once you know which block a name belongs to.

statement:
This program is meant to read a temperature, convert it, and print the result. It compiles with no errors, runs, and prints the wrong number every time.

The bug is **one line**, and it is not a typo in any expression — every line here does exactly what it says. Click the line that causes the wrong answer.
hints: There is nothing wrong with the arithmetic. Look instead at how many variables called `fahrenheit` this program has.
A declaration inside a block creates a *new* variable, even if a variable with that name already exists outside the block. The inner one hides the outer one until the block ends.
Which line makes a second variable where the author meant to assign to the first?

payload.prompt: Click the line that causes the wrong answer.
